Perfume rating 4.10 out of 5 with 4,953 votes

Dama Bianca by Xerjoff is a Floral Woody Musk fragrance for women. Dama Bianca was launched in 2012. Top notes are Kumquat and Lime; middle notes are Violet, Italian Iris, Lilac, Egyptian Jasmine and Lily-of-the-Valley; base notes are Vanilla, Malt, White Musk, Ambrette (Musk Mallow), Sandalwood and Cedar.

suzanne_ronald 12/10/25 06:22

Ethereal Purple Flowers with Fruity Accents and a Malty Vanilla Base...

Powdery & succulent violet steals the show here, all blue skinned and dressed in powdery white, . This beauty opens with a burst of tropical citrus (kumquat & lime) and deepens into a succulent violet-iris-vanilla heart resting on a balmy & malty vanilla base. In the air I get the violets - so succulent they are almost like blueberries - and on the skin I get balmy vanilla and powdery iris florals.

This type of base can sometimes become too sweet on me, but there's a root-y earthy facet here, and the purple flowers & fruits keep it from becoming too sweet. Aside from dupes (like Junoon Noir Al Haramain), I find the base here very similar to the bases of non-dupe scents like Gentle Fluidity Gold MFK, Intense Cafe Montale, Ristretto Intense Cafe Montale, Crystal Rose Swiss Arabian, Velvet Gold Orientica & Vanilla Romance Bath & Body Works. Overall: Well above average performance with amazing scent profile, it's a love. Enjoy!

Contrast to Junoon Noir Al Haramain:
This is a dupe of Dama Bianca with good approximation & excellent performance. I have a hard time telling them apart side by side, but it seems like Junoon Noir may be drying down ever so slightly sweeter. Out of the gate Dama Bianca had superior performance, but as time goes on, Junoon Noir is developing a beast mode performance.

Contrast to Gentle Fluidity Gold Maison Francis Kurkjian:
These are different, but there's a similarity in the malty vanilla base. Dama Bianca has purple flowers up top, while Gentle Fluidity Gold has juniper berries. Both have good performance.

Contrast to Vanilla Romance Bath & Body Works:
These are different, but again there's a similarity in the malty vanilla base. Dama Bianca has the purple flowers up top, while Vanilla Romance has cardamom. Vanilla Romance doesn't have as strong of performance as Dama Bianca, which is what you'd expect from a body mist, although Vanilla Romance has above average performance for a mist.

wirthgeo 07/22/25 06:22

The fragrance that shattered all my preconceived notions.
I used to roll my eyes at vanilla-based perfumes — “too common”, avoided powdery scents — “too matronly”, and stayed away from anything overly feminine.
And then...BOOM: I find my signature scent in a composition that’s primarily powdery-vanilla and unmistakably designed for women.

I adore how it evolves on my skin:
It starts off sparkling with citrus, then within minutes I'm awash in nostalgia from the violet notes. At the same time, a clean, delicate floral freshness emerges thanks to the white flowers, eventually giving way to a sensual base of amber, woods, and vanilla.
The only note I detect from start to finish is the malt — for me, it adds to that nostalgic yet completely unique atmosphere, holding together something elusive and hard to define. Very subtly, it’s like high-quality beer spilled on and soaked into a cedarwood table.

All of this blends into an ethereal, gentle, slightly melancholic, sparklingly fragile, and special fragrance.
The soft projection and sillage — which some might consider a downside — I see as a strength. I prefer skin-close scents in general, but this perfume especially benefits from not bursting through doors or leaving a loud trail behind. It just quietly envelops you in a soft, angelic aura.

It’s ambivalent — part of me wants to shout it from the rooftops and make everyone smell it when I wear it, but at the same time, I want to keep it to myself and my inner circle, because it feels so intimate.
Longevity is about 6–7 hours on my skin, and days on clothing.
Bonus points — or rather, a gold star — for the design, which perfectly matches the essence of what’s inside the bottle.

tonileefiore 04/09/25 14:11

I am editing my original review after purchasing a 100ml bottle of Dama Bianca. I've applied the fragrance regularly over the course of several days now. I initially reviewed the fragrance after using a sizable decant sample.

Dama Bianca is a pretty, fruity-woody-floral-vanilla fragrance with an interesting yeast-y, malt-like accord. The iris flower gives the fragrance a pretty, powdery soft nuance. The balance of the many notes is well-done. IMHO, Dama Blanca is definitely a fragrance with mixed florals at its core.

The opening is clearly an unusual citrus blast of kumquat and lime, I suppose. The middle development is exactly as described in the notes: a medley of gentle purple and white florals. The base is vanilla, wood, musk and malt. Malt gives the fragrance a thicker, yeast-like dry-down.

Feminine, ethereal, ephemeral, veil-like, wispy. I love the fragrance's allure. I just wish it had greater performance both in projection and longevity.

And now that I own a full-bottle , I'm realizing over-spraying is the enemy. When applied lightly, the perfume's performance is nice. Over-applying turns the fragrance into a suffocating, floral mess.

Not sure I'm loving it as much as I did when sampling.

luvoxlixir 02/22/25 03:23

Dama Bianca drapes itself in pale lilac and vanilla-laced musk, its ethereal presence both delicate and curiously substantial. The lilac here is a key player on my skin. Not exactly a photorealistic bloom, but softened, powdered petals infused with violet's dewy whisper, its coumarinic sweetness folding into the scent. That quick glint of citrus in the opening is pretty too, tart kumquat lending a ghostly vibrance before fading into the pillowy expanse of orris. Not buttery but more starchy, this woody orris base stretches into the air like weightless threads, a nutty vanilla emerging below it.

DB is not gourmand, its composition is more sweet nutty floral than outright confection, airy roundness swelling slightly against a base of white woods and ambrette’s musky, slightly fruity hum. A porcelain-toned abstraction of lilac fields and ground wheat, sifted through cold air.

Then last night at 11:30 he was grinning like a chesire cat, insisting that he couldn't wait til Valentine's Day to give me my present. Obviously I eagerly relented. He pulls out this neatly wrapped, teal, package tied with a teal ribbon. I saved the ribbon but tore into the paper...

I nearly cried tears of joy when I opened a brand new 100ml box of Dama Bianca in it's lovely velvet lined presentation box!
When I first tested it months ago and fell in love with it's magical scent I didn't think he noticed... THAT glorious aroma of white wine spiked, white-hot chocolate that melts to powdery white irises, white parma violets mingled with vanilla malt and a hint of citrus?! His response? "I know my Baby very well. And know what makes her happy." Turns out he had already made up his mind to get me a bottle well before I dropped any hints! So I will be wearing my beloved new present to dinner on Valentine's Day! I have the world's best husband. ♡

ginandrice 11/11/20 02:50

This might be the softest, fluffiest sweet scent I’ve ever smelled. It’s tipsy angels in flower crowns, giggling over a platter of powdered donuts. It’s a lazy morning with sweet cereal milk and puffy down blankets. It’s the melted white goo of a Rice Crispie treat before you mix the Rice Crispies in.

It’s innocent, happy, and weightless—the smell of a softer world.

There isn’t one single edge to this fragrance. Not even the lime has any sharpness. And if I hadn’t seen the notes list, I couldn’t tell you a single thing in it, except probably the vanilla, and even that is unusually rich and malty. (The color scheme of the bottle represents this fragrance perfectly.)

This is definitely one of my favorites from the Casamorati line, though somewhat lacking in sillage.

umma toga 12/05/18 12:26

This is one of the best fragrances I've ever had the pleasure of smelling. It smells like the most delicate floral mix with violet dominating, and a gorgeous boozy malty vanilla and a helping of powdery white musk. To put it simply, It smells like a more refined cologne of the missions mixed with a violet-iris-lipstick scent. It is pretty strong for such a soft, ethereal scent too. I just love it.

Soofiya 05/13/17 09:12

Xerjoff dama biyanca isn't easy to find comparing to others so today when I saw a tester of it in a perfume shop I couldn't wait to ask SA to test it on my skin.
As soon as he sprayed it,I could smell this fluffy vanilla which was very pleasant.I knew that I will need a bottle.I can't describe scent development so I will edit as soon as I can give it a proper test,for now the only thing I can say is that it was different from what I had imagined.I imagined it to be a powdery Musky vanilla in the league of armani lei or Jil sander Jil.it IS a powdery Musky vanilla scent but it also has some gourmand facets.not gourmand in a foody way just sweet and delicious.citrus notes didn't show up on my skin.neither did violet.it felt very familiar and finally I remembered which perfume it's reminding me.le couvens des minimes cologne of the missions.call me crazy but these two are very similar to my nose.the same warm caramelized and cozy vanilla,they same smokey myrrh deliciousness but dama biyanca is softer,powdery and less intensely sweet.dama bianca seems to be a more feminine and classy sister
I think I can name myself a xerjoff fan as I have and love lira,bouquet ideal,mefisto and granballo and now I'm loving dama biyanca and will save to buy it ASAP.I believe xerjoff has an amazing ability in creating great feminine sweet scents,makes them balanced,grownup,memorable and intresting
If you'd like a soft but also longlasting veil of vanilla and powder,something delicious in a grown up way,comforting and cuddly give it a try
Just one spray remained strong for a long time. Now after seven hour it's still there but lightly
Edit: I finally bought it but forgot to edit my review.I still like it a lot.
Dama Bianca is a combination of sweet,yummy and boozy vanilla+powder(I can't pickup violet or iris individually but I def can pickup tones of powder)+malt(I believe this is what makes it original)+musk/ambrette+soft,non-descript florals+creamy and subtle woody notes
It's very pleasant,smooth,comforting,memorable,addictive and beautiful.I have a friend who believes it leans toward being masculine but I disagree as I find Dama Bianca a superfeminine peefume.one can match it with a white,beige and golden silk dress and if you're looking for a non-floral bride perfume,you have to give it a try.
It's soft and gentle but I like the fact that it keeps it's strength for hours,unlike most of other perfumes which punch you in face when first sprayed and fade away into nothingness after an hour
Highly recommended if sweet powdery boozy vanilla seems appealing to you
داما بیانکا ترکیبی از وانیل+مالت(که بنظرم مسئول رایحه به یادموندنی این عطره)+پودر(من مقادیر زیادی پودر ازش میگیرم اما زنبق و بنفشه برام بصورت نت های مستقل قابل تشخیص نیستن)+مشک تمیز و لطیف هست و در پس زمینه روایح گلی و چوبی ملایم و خامه ای هم حضور دارن.من هیچ مرکباتی ازش نمیگیرم،فقط یه رایحه خوشمزه،پودری و مشروبی
داما بیانکا گرم،دلنشین،آرامش بخش،فمینین و باکلاسه،با یه پیراهن حریر سفید،بژ و طلایی بخوبی ست میشه و اگه دنبال یه عطر عروس غیرگلی و
متفاوت هستید گزینه عالی هست
درمجموع عطر ملایمیه بااینحال ضعیف نیست و تا ساعتها قدرت اولیه ی خودش رو حفظ میکنه
بنظر من برند زرجوف و ب ویژه لاین کازاموراتی پر از عطرهای زنانه فوق العاده ست که داما بیانکا یکی از اونهاسا
